name: Yola

ancestors.notes: Descent from Middle English (South-West Midland input); Dolan & Ó Muirithe (1996)

notes: Skeleton. Yola (extinct English variety of Forth and Bargy, County Wexford), descended from Middle English. Idiosyncratic 18th-19th c. orthography; a broad English-like grapheme map is used and the elided leading apostrophe (e.g. 'cha) is unencoded. High PER expected. Stress exemption: Yola (the Forth and Bargy dialect of English) inherits English's lexical, non-orthography-predictable stress; the 18th-19th century antiquarian spellings recorded by Jacob Poole and analyzed by Dolan & Ó Muirithe do not mark it. Source: Dolan, T. P. & Ó Muirithe, Diarmaid (1996), The Dialect of Forth and Bargy. The wikipron/yol gold is not attested speech: every entry's IPA is what Wiktionary editors supply under a 'Yola phonology' pronunciation key, applied to spellings taken from the same 1867 Poole & Barnes glossary this spec cites (verified 2026 by fetching https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cowm, whose References section cites Jacob Poole, ed. William Barnes, 'A Glossary...of the old Dialect of the English Colony in the Baronies of Forth and Bargy' (1867), https://books.google.com/books?id=KBEHAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA32, and whose Pronunciation line links '(key)' to the English Wikipedia 'Yola phonology' article). yol/wikipron is therefore an agreement row, the same category as the epitran- and espeak-derived golds in docs/benchmarks.md: a low PER measures conformance to Wiktionary editors' reconstruction rules, not accuracy against Yola as spoken, and no gold for an extinct language with no recordings can be otherwise. The gold also carries substantial inherent ambiguity from Poole's non-standardised 18th-19th c. spelling: 444 of the 1972 distinct spellings (22.5%, the highest homograph rate measured in this campaign) have two or more mutually incompatible gold transcriptions for the identical string -- consistent with a reconstruction applied by many hands to inconsistent nineteenth-century spelling -- so a meaningful share of the PER gap is not recoverable by any deterministic spec.
